title: Deterministic physics rule-list transfer on 160 OOD human labels
why: The deterministic rule list (L1.23) was degenerate in-domain; test whether a frozen, thresholded physics rule list transfers out-of-domain on the 160 human Egocentric-10K labels, and which rules survive the shift.
hypothesis: Quality tripwires (blur, entropy, sharpness) transfer; activity/semantic rules may not.
data: 160 Egocentric-10K human windows (138/22, 47 factories; labels/ood160_labels.json); physics+theory per-window features (frozen 160x90 recipe); frozen IndEgo rule table (configs/perpixel_v1.json + rulelist.json, B/verify-rules)
method: apply frozen IndEgo thresholds (Q=4, no OOD fitting); OR rule list; AUROC + balanced accuracy with factory-grouped bootstrap (n_boot=2000); per-rule precision/recall; review-band frontier

summary: Frozen deterministic rule list does NOT transfer. R3 (perpixel_v1 quality stage: lowent,blur,ten) OOD AUROC 0.475 [0.327,0.630] grouped, bal.acc 0.441 [0.325,0.581], rejects 60/160, false-accept 16/22, false-reject 54/138. R5 (active: blur,lowent,ten,madfroz,pbytes) AUROC 0.493 [0.349,0.636], BA 0.456. Below chance and worse than the frozen logistic baseline 0.566 [0.424,0.700]/0.546. Review band makes BA monotonically worse (0.456 -> 0.049 at 84% review). Per-rule: lowent/frozen/ffroz/still abstain (0 fires); blur/ten/dark/lowsnr/overexp/pbytes/clipfrac misfire (OOD precision 0.03-0.18, must abstain); only madfroz has >chance precision (0.333, recall 0.09). Absolute IndEgo thresholds do not carry across the resolution/codec shift.
decision: Do not ship the deterministic physics rule list as an OOD gate, not even as a review tripwire. Keep lowent/frozen/ffroz/still as abstain-only no-ops; gate with the adapted per-pixel model (O2/O4). Re-derive any absolute threshold per regime.
cost: CPU; 160 windows x physics+theory (170 s, 2 workers); no GPU
